children: Gold's powerful August rally is running into a new obstacle as rising oil prices and a suddenly more hawkish Federal Reserve push Treasury yields higher. Gold futures fell to a nearly two-week low Monday, and losses deepened Tuesday, showing that even escalating Middle East tensions are struggling to offset the pressure from higher interest-rate expectations.
Front-month Comex gold for September delivery fell
1% to $4,431.10 an ounce Monday
, its lowest settlement since August 18. Silver dropped
1.1% to $66.221 an ounce
. The pullback came despite an exceptionally strong August, when gold climbed
and silver surged
The pressure intensified after renewed U.S.-Iran military clashes pushed crude oil prices higher, reviving fears that energy costs could keep inflation elevated. Brent crude settled above
$90 a barrel Monday
, while Treasury yields climbed as investors reassessed the outlook for monetary policy.

That matters for gold because the metal pays no interest. Rising bond yields increase the opportunity cost of holding bullion, while tighter Fed policy can strengthen the dollar and make dollar-denominated gold more expensive for overseas buyers.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh added to that pressure at Jackson Hole by signaling policymakers could have more work to do if inflation fails to return toward the central bank's 2% goal. Markets subsequently lifted the probability of a
September rate hike to roughly two-thirds
, compared with 36% before his remarks.
Gold extended its retreat Tuesday, with spot prices dropping more than 1% toward
$4,386 an ounce
as Treasury yields continued climbing.
Investors Takeaway
The immediate test is U.S. labor data. The
August jobs report arrives September 4
, followed by producer-price data on September 10 and CPI on September 11.

Weak employment numbers could cool rate-hike expectations and relieve pressure on gold. Strong jobs or stubborn inflation, however, could drive yields and the dollar higher and extend the correction. Investors should therefore watch
Treasury yields, Fed rate-hike probabilities, oil prices and the dollar
alongside geopolitical developments. Gold's strong August gains leave the longer-term rally intact, but the Fed has suddenly become its biggest near-term test.

title: Gold's Powerful Rally Runs Into a New Wall
